clue.text: Woman's success if adopting a left-wing stance

indicators.note: adopting here means taking on what follows, so the next piece is attached directly after

parts.note: a success is a win
red is the colour of the political left, so a left-wing stance is red

explanation.surface: A woman succeeds by moving to the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: Winifred is a female given name, so a woman's name fits the definition.

clue.text: Think I'm not in favour of energy

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written
agin is a dialect word for against, so not in favour
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone considers themselves opposed to the energy sector.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is an old dialect form of 'against', common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture or suppose something is to think it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Complexity confounded any critic

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the next words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky work baffled every reviewer who tried it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' looks like a verb with 'Complexity' as its subject, but it signals the rearrangement of ANY CRITIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate detail makes something complicated, so the noun is a synonym for complexity.

clue.text: Raised some of these tariffs making payment to council

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone raised their charges when paying the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raised' means read upwards, so the hidden SETAR, spanning 'theSE TARiffs', is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, rates were the local property tax paid to the council before council tax.

clue.text: Determined daughter getting seated after a struggle

indicators.note: after a struggle suggests the letters of seated have been wrestled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl finally got sitting down after resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a struggle' looks like timing in the story but signals the anagram EADSET; 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead set on something means being firmly resolved, an idiom for determined.

clue.text: Redirect Queen entering European parliament

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament, a European one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A monarch visits a parliament in Europe and changes its course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil Éireann is Ireland's lower house.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something off its intended track is to send it elsewhere, so redirect is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Evidence of mishap is leading attempt to provide medical treatment

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the word is comes ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a dent in a car is a sign of an accident
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A sign of an accident prompts an effort to give someone care.
explanation.definitionFit: Work on teeth is a branch of healthcare, so it counts as medical treatment.

clue.text: Soldiers collapse after blocking one later appearance

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: after blocking means once something is kept out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to ruin is to collapse or fall down
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops fall apart after stopping a single opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' here means keeping a letter out rather than putting one in, which is the usual sense in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat showing of a programme is a later appearance of it on screen.

clue.text: Find room for popular item like this, after intervention by Director

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: intervention means coming between, so the letter goes into the middle of the word

parts.note: this item in the puzzle is a clue

explanation.surface: A director's meddling makes space for a favourite piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item like this' is self-referential: the thing you are reading is a CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make space for something in a group or list is to count it in, a synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle requiring constant skill

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Some vehicle needs steady expertise to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled wagon pulled by a horse or pushed by hand is a vehicle.

clue.text: Macabre situation in West about to block railway?

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the way, so these pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: railway lines are track
W is the compass abbreviation for west
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Something grim out west is stopping trains running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece of the wordplay, not a link word; the question mark marks the loose, figurative definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster people cannot look away from is a grim spectacle, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Names, including island locations

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: to name a source is to cite it, so names means cites

explanation.surface: A list of names takes in an island's places.
explanation.definitionFit: Large towns are places on a map, so they are locations by example.

clue.text: Historical leader, English, brought in token European

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: a token is a sign
EUR is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An English figure from history introduced a symbolic European.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal lord in old France held power over his estate, so he was a historical leader.

clue.text: US uniform symbol regressive goon allowed on both sides of uniform

indicators.note: on both sides of means flanking, so the letter sits between the two pieces
regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an ape is a brutish lout, a goon
let means allowed
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American badge is worn by a backward thug either side of his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling has one T; British English often writes EPAULETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder ornament on military dress marks rank, so it is a symbol on a uniform.

clue.text: Story: good part elevated Duke, a feudal nobleman

parts.note: a story can be a lie

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means raised up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A tale in which a fine role raised up a duke to noble rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior to whom vassals owed allegiance was a feudal nobleman.

clue.text: Tense chap dismissing first bank employee

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: dismissing first means losing the opening letter of the word

parts.note: feller is a colloquial word for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A nervous man sacks the top worker at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the chap, but it gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier at a bank counter who takes and pays out money is a bank employee.

clue.text: Sly look around cool street in British city

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the other pieces go inside this word

parts.note: a leer is a sly or knowing look
ice is something cool, or to cool something

explanation.surface: Someone gives a knowing glance around a chilly street in a UK city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English East Midlands, so it is a British city.

clue.text: Limits to another gaudy line in fabric design

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: There are bounds to how many more flashy stripes a fabric pattern can take.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond pattern used in knitted socks and sweaters is a fabric design.

clue.text: Ill-feeling spread, attaching to most of monarch's circle

parts.note: ink that spread ran

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: a king's court is the circle around the monarch

explanation.surface: Bad blood spread through nearly all of the royal entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attaching to' just joins RAN to COUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter lasting resentment is a strong form of ill-feeling, a synonym.

clue.text: Delightful state is unknown in obstinate bloke, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the whole is read backwards
in means placed inside, so these letters go within the word

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A stubborn man, looking back, finds bliss in mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obstinate bloke' is a mule, the crossword's usual stubborn animal used of a person; 'on reflection' turns the whole assembly round, not just the mule.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the paradise of the blessed dead, so it names a state of bliss.

clue.text: Each will surmount small incline in part of London?

indicators.note: will surmount means will sit on top, which in a down clue puts this piece first

parts.note: to incline towards something is to tend

explanation.surface: Each person will climb a little slope in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example. The East End is the traditional working-class area east of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This district east of the City is one area of the capital, so it is part of the city.

clue.text: Rodents seen around old New England in geological epoch

indicators.note: seen around means appearing on both sides, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: Mice were spotted around old New England in some prehistoric era.
explanation.definitionFit: The period roughly 23 to 5 million years ago is a division of geological time.

clue.text: Newspaper items recommending spaying?

definitions.meaning: short cuttings or brief extracts from the press
split in two, the word is an instruction to neuter animals: a cut for household companions

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a piece advising readers to neuter their animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into SNIP, a cut, and PETS, giving an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Small scraps of news or text are short pieces, the sense behind newspaper items.

clue.text: Current item I dropped in support of the old man's ways

indicators.note: in support of means underneath, which in a down clue puts the earlier piece on top

parts.note: pa is a father, the old man

indicators.note: dropped means let fall, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: this means the current one, as in this week

explanation.surface: A modern gadget, now ditched, backs up Dad's customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks and routes are ways to walk, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Suppress hurry, eradicating it

indicators.note: eradicating means wiping out, so the word it is removed from the phrase

parts.note: the urging phrase to put your foot down on the accelerator means hurry

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry up and stamp something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' appears twice in effect: the phrase for hurry ends in IT, and 'eradicating it' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush or squash something underfoot is to suppress it, an idiom.

clue.text: Small objects, not medium in places

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: items are objects
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: Little things, not mid-sized ones, fill certain spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations where things stand or happen are places, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Working with trustee in secret dispute

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the word

parts.note: covert means secret
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone collaborates with a trustee in a secret argument.
explanation.walkthrough: TR for trustee is a dictionary abbreviation rarely seen outside crosswords; 'with' only joins the two inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue against or deny a claim is to dispute it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Push to give up Times, after reflection — saving this?

indicators.note: after reflection means mirrored, so the remaining letters are read backwards
to give up means to surrender, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to exert yourself is to push hard
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A campaign urges people to stop buying The Times to save the forests.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping X from EXERT leaves EERT, which 'after reflection' reverses. The definition refers back to the whole clue: giving up a paper saves trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is made from wood pulp, so not buying a paper saves timber: the thing being saved.

clue.text: Removed evidence of periods of French backsliding

parts.note: eras are periods of history

indicators.note: backsliding means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: Traces of French history slipping back were wiped away.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out so no trace remains is to remove all sign of it.

clue.text: Just half-dead — beginning to rally — then died

indicators.note: half means taking the first two of the word's four letters

parts.note: in tennis a serve begins each rally

explanation.surface: A player half-dead started a comeback, then expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is the adjective, as in a just reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair or merited outcome is one that was earned, so the adjective matches just.
